title: K-flat realization of the augmented derived scalar-extension tower
statement:
Let $C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $a_n:R\to B_n$ and $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ maps of sheaves of commutative rings for $n\ge1$, with $b_na_{n+1}=a_n$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories and localizations $Q_R,Q_{B_n}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F_n=-\otimes_R^L B_n$, $G_n=-\otimes_{B_{n+1}}^L B_n$ for K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $r_n:D(B_n)\to D(R)$, $j_n:D(B_n)\to D(B_{n+1})$ for exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Give these functors the normalized derived tensor/restriction adjunctions $F_n\dashv r_n$ and $G_n\dashv j_n$ of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]; let $u_n:\mathrm{id}\to r_nF_n$ be their units. Let $\alpha_n:G_nF_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_n$ be the canonical scalar-composition comparison [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. For $K\in D(R)$ let $\delta_n(K):F_{n+1}K\to j_nF_nK$ be the adjoint of $\alpha_n(K)$. Define $d_n(K):r_{n+1}F_{n+1}K\to r_nF_nK$ by applying $r_{n+1}$ to $\delta_n(K)$ and using the identity-on-underlying-sheaves comparison $r_{n+1}j_n\cong r_n$.

Let $P$ be a K-flat $R$-complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $e:Q_R(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ an isomorphism. Put $T_n(P)=\operatorname{Res}_{a_n}(P\otimes_RB_n)$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with strict maps $t_n(p\otimes b)=p\otimes b_n(b)$ and $c_n(p)=p\otimes1$. The canonical K-flat computation comparisons, transported along $F_n(e^{-1})$ and then restricted, give isomorphisms
$$\epsilon_n:r_nF_nK\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(T_n(P))$$
satisfying
$$\epsilon_n\circ u_n(K)\circ e=Q_R(c_n),\qquad
\epsilon_n\circ d_n(K)=Q_R(t_n)\circ\epsilon_{n+1}.$$
These comparisons are natural for chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives and respect every composite quotient transition. No flatness or surjectivity of $a_n$ or $b_n$, and no boundedness of $P$, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent refinement retaining the K-flat computation comparisons, derived adjunction units and quotient transition maps simultaneously.

proof.text: Write $M_n=P\otimes_R B_n$ and $X=Q_R(P)$. The balanced map $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes b_n(s)$ defines a morphism $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{b_n}M_n$: the balancing identity holds because $b_na_{n+1}=a_n$. Tensor here is sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, so the compatible sectionwise maps induce sheaf maps. They commute with differentials, since both differentials send $p\otimes s$ to $d_P(p)\otimes s$. Scalar restriction leaves the underlying abelian sheaf and map unchanged. Thus restriction gives exactly $t_n$, and $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ gives $c_n$. The identity $b_n(1)=1$ gives $t_nc_{n+1}=c_n$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, identity-topos specialization; sheaf tensor as defined in sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EK

proof.text: For each $n$, the K-flat computation of derived change of rings gives the canonical isomorphism $\gamma_n:F_nX\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{B_n}(M_n)$. Exact scalar restriction commutes with the localizations, as in the derived coefficient adjunction. Write $\rho_n=r_n(\gamma_n):r_nF_nX\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(T_n(P))$, using that comparison. Define $\epsilon_n=\rho_n\circ r_nF_n(e^{-1})$. These are isomorphisms; no resolution of the coefficient sheaf $B_n$ is required, because $P$ is K-flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; canonical K-flat computation

proof.text: The normalized adjunction for $a_n$ identifies the unit at $X$ with $p\mapsto p\otimes1$; hence $\rho_n\circ u_n(X)=Q_R(c_n)$. Naturality of that unit at $e:X\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ gives $r_nF_n(e^{-1})\circ u_n(K)\circ e=u_n(X)$. Composing with $\rho_n$ proves $\epsilon_n\circ u_n(K)\circ e=Q_R(c_n)$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, normalized unit on a K-flat representative; derived.tex Tags 0FND and 09T5

proof.text: Apply K-flat pullback preservation to the identity topos with coefficient map $a_{n+1}$. Its hypotheses hold because $C$ is small and $P$ is K-flat with flat terms. It gives that $M_{n+1}$ is K-flat over $B_{n+1}$ with flat terms. Consequently both $G_nF_{n+1}X$ and $F_nX$ are computed on the ordinary complexes used in the scalar-composition comparison. Its representative is $A_n:(M_{n+1}\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n)\to M_n$, $(p\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto p\otimes b_n(s)t$, with the inverse specified by that comparison. This is the stipulated $\alpha_n(X)$ under the computation isomorphisms, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between its source and target.

For an adjunction $G_n\dashv j_n$, the adjunct of a map $h:G_nY\to Z$ is $j_n(h)\circ\eta^b_Y$, where $\eta^b$ is its unit. Apply this to $h=\alpha_n(X)$. By the normalized unit formula, on the representative $M_{n+1}$ this composite sends $p\otimes s$ first to $(p\otimes s)\otimes1$ and then, by $A_n$, to $p\otimes b_n(s)$. Thus $\delta_n(X)$ is the class of the sheaf map in Step 1 under $\gamma_{n+1}$ and $\gamma_n$. Restricting scalars therefore gives $\rho_n\circ d_n(X)=Q_R(t_n)\circ\rho_{n+1}$. Naturality of the Hom correspondence and of $\alpha_n$ gives naturality of $\delta_n$, hence of $d_n$. In particular $r_nF_n(e^{-1})\circ d_n(K)=d_n(X)\circ r_{n+1}F_{n+1}(e^{-1})$. Compose the preceding representative equality with $r_{n+1}F_{n+1}(e^{-1})$ to obtain $\epsilon_n\circ d_n(K)=Q_R(t_n)\circ\epsilon_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, normalized unit and natural Hom correspondence; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: For a chain map $f:P\to P'$ between the stated representatives, the canonical K-flat computation comparison is natural: $Q_{B_n}(f\otimes1)\circ\gamma_n(P)=\gamma_n(P')\circ F_n(Q_Rf)$. This is the comparison natural transformation of the left derived functor, restricted to K-flat objects. Restriction gives the same square for $\rho_n$. The strict tensor maps commute as well: both orders send $p\otimes s$ to $f(p)\otimes b_n(s)$, and the unit square sends $p$ to $f(p)\otimes1$. Transport along chosen representative isomorphisms therefore gives the asserted naturality of $\epsilon_n$. For $m>n$, the strict composite sends $p\otimes s$ to $p\otimes(b_n\cdots b_{m-1})(s)$. Inductively compose the adjacent equalities of Step 5 to get $\epsilon_n d_{n,m}=Q_R(t_{n,m})\epsilon_m$, with identities when $m=n$. The iterated scalar-composition comparisons agree and are natural in the ring maps, so this composite is also the transition defined directly using the comparison for $B_m\to B_n$; the mate calculation is again $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes(b_n\cdots b_{m-1})(s)$. This proves compatibility for every composite, together with the augmentation identity of Step 1.

tool_uses.why: Generic K-flat computation of derived scalar extension, needed for each ring map; this unit does not reconstruct the derived functor.
